title: A New Radio to Overcome Critical Link Budgets

predicted_errors.error_location: Section III.A, line 43: 'coherent combining of N² entries at the receiver to N data symbols can result in an N-fold gain in received power'; also line 60: 'For T=N, the same combining gain as with transmit beamforming is achieved'; line 168: '12.0 dB combining gain of transmit beamforming with 16 antennas'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper states transmit beamforming gain as N (e.g., 10·log₁₀(16)=12.0 dB), but coherent combining of N antenna signals at a single receiver gives amplitude gain N and power gain N² (24.1 dB for N=16). Temporal combining correctly uses T-fold gain (noise accumulates), but spatial beamforming combines before receiver noise — hence N². Confirmed by: (a) SPOT ground truth, (b) author's own arXiv withdrawal note ('should be N²'), (c) corrected companion paper v3. This error propagates through claims about 'no loss in link budget gain' (abstract), 'comparing favorably' (line 168), and the K-user equivalence analysis (line 268).

predicted_errors.error_location: Line 3: 'MA-TISK does not suffer from spectral re-growth issues plaguing other constant envelope modulations like GMSK.'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: GMSK (BT=0.3) is specifically designed for compact spectrum with constant envelope and is widely used in GSM precisely because it avoids significant spectral regrowth. Spectral regrowth is an out-of-band emission problem driven by amplitude nonlinearities, which constant-envelope GMSK avoids by design. Characterizing GMSK as 'plagued' by spectral regrowth is technically questionable. The paper provides no reference or evidence for this claim.

predicted_errors.error_location: Line 19: 'Heisenberg's Uncertainty Principle prohibits a signal to be well-constrained in both time and frequency.'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: This refers to the time-bandwidth (Gabor) uncertainty relation in signal processing, not the quantum-mechanical Heisenberg uncertainty principle. While 'Heisenberg uncertainty' is sometimes used as engineering shorthand for this trade-off (the paper itself uses the correct term 'Heisenberg's time-frequency uncertainty' at line 280), the reference to the quantum principle is imprecise. The underlying trade-off is valid and the error has no impact on the paper's conclusions.

summary: This paper (arXiv 2402.10307v2, later withdrawn by the author with the note 'The paper is not correct') contains a critical mathematical error at its core: the transmit beamforming gain is calculated as N-fold when the correct physics gives N²-fold power gain. This error propagates through multiple claims — the abstract's assertion of 'no loss in link budget gain,' the numerical comparisons in Section IV (12.0 dB vs. correct 24.1 dB for N=16), and the K-user equivalence argument in Section IV.C. Beyond this, the paper has significant structural issues: Sections I, II, and V are entirely missing; 5 inline citations ([5]-[9]) have no reference entries; bullet point formatting is corrupted with two items missing; a sentence is fragmented across non-consecutive lines; figures are referenced out of numerical order; two bibliographic entries contain factual errors (wrong journal name for [23], misspelled author for [25]); and a technically dubious claim characterizes GMSK as 'plagued by spectral re-growth.' The paper's equations (1), (2), (4), (9), (10) are individually correct, and the MA-TISK concept as presented is internally consistent — all errors stem from the incorrect beamforming gain premise and incomplete/broken formatting.
